newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico textile tariffs help small firms - industry.
newsitem.headline: Mexico textile tariffs help small firms - industry.

text.p: Tariffs on imported textiles unveiled by the Mexican government last week were a limited measure necessary to protect small domestic businesses, an industry spokesman told reporters on Thursday.

"The safeguard system...will not be activated until some products reach the threshold of 1994 imports. We are talking about 70 percent for some items, and 80 percent for others," said Edmond Kuri, president of the Mexican Textile Industry Chamber (Canaintex).

The Trade and Industry Ministry (Secofi) last week announced import tariffs of 15-25 percent for 49 categories of textiles. The tariffs apply mostly to synthetic fabrics and are outside the scope of Mexico's international trade agreements.
Imports to Mexico of textiles and many items boomed in 1994 on what many have since acknowledged to have been an overvalued currency.
The new tariffs are part of a government program to promote micro, small and medium-sized businesses, which account for 95 percent of some 2,200 textile firms in Mexico.
Kuri said that without the program, idle production capacity in the textile industry could increase by 30-50 percent.
